summary: Small screen-marker helper that follows one world actor: it keeps the actor pointer at +0x28, copies the actor position into the lazily allocated 0x98-byte marker visual and hides it when the actor is hidden or too far away.
evidence: maybe_Ui_Marker_FollowActor 0x003BC030 dereferences self->f_28 as an actor (position +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4, hidden +0x2F0, distance limit +0x320) and lazily allocates the 0x98-byte marker visual; maybe_Ui_Marker_RetryBindTarget 0x003BC418 throttles a retry counter at +8. The 'Marker' label is only moderately supported because 0x004A06E0 was re-attributed to Gfx_BuildSegmentBasis.

fields.name: targetActor
fields.evidence: self->f_28 is dereferenced as a Field_Actor: f_9c/f_a0/f_a4 are its f32 world position (Field_Actor +0x9C..+0xA4), +0x2F0 is the hidden flag and +0x320 the follow distance limit; Ui_Marker_FollowActor passes it to func_0017CB68/func_0017C8C4.

summary: Input/state handler for the message window's confirm/cancel flow: it asks the UI core whether the child screen was hit and then advances the state object at +0x13C to state 10 (confirm) or 5 (cancel).
evidence: maybe_Ui_MessageScreen_HandleConfirm 0x002F60DC and maybe_Ui_MessageScreen_HandleCancel 0x002F6670 both query the UI core's child screen (Ui_GetCore()->f_14->f_C through vtable +0x18) and on a hit call vtable +0x18 of the object at self+0x13C with 10 / 5; the class exists only as these two 76-byte handlers plus one wrapper, so the label is kept but not proven.

fields.name: maybe_stateMachine
fields.evidence: The object at +0x13C receives integer states through its vtable slot +0x18 - '(**(code **)(*self->f_13c + 0x18))(self->f_13c,10);' in HandleConfirm and the same call with 5 in HandleCancel - so it is the message screen's state target; its concrete class is not identified, hence maybe_.

summary: Message-window text renderer: a Ui window base whose initialiser stores the class vtable at +0 and constructs a Ui_Object text sub-object (with its own vtable) at +0x70.
evidence: Ui_MessageTextRenderer_Init 0x00393318 calls Ui_WindowBase_Ctor, builds a Ui_Object at +0x70 with Ui_Object_CtorWithPriority, stores DAT_0039333C+0x9C in that sub-object's vtable slot and writes the main vtable (DAT_0039333C = 0x00766C10) back at +0 through 'piVar2[-0x1c]'; its caller is Ui_SetupMessageWindow 0x0027D108.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: The initialiser writes the class vtable pointer at offset 0 ('piVar2[-0x1c] = iVar1;' with iVar1 = 0x00766C10 = DAT_0039333C) while installing the sub-object vtable DAT_0039333C+0x9C at +0x70, so +0 is the polymorphic base's vtable.

summary: Owner/cache record for one loaded UI layout pack: the pack handle lives at +0x828 and LoadLayout/LoadLayoutChecked/UnloadLayout open, replace and release it.
evidence: maybe_Ui_Pack_LoadLayout 0x004546A8 builds '<name>.pack' (s__s_pack_00454B68), loads it with Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple and swaps the new handle into self+0x828 after freeing the previous one through Pack_FreeHandleEntry; Ui_Pack_LoadLayoutChecked 0x00454880 is the same chain with an early 0 return; Ui_Pack_UnloadLayout 0x00455684 calls Pack_ReleaseHandle(self+0x828).

fields.name: packHandle
fields.evidence: self->f_828 is a packed handle: slot = handle & 0xFFF indexes the 0x007BA2D0 table (stride 8) and generation = handle >> 12; it is freed by Pack_FreeHandleEntry and released by Pack_ReleaseHandle(self + 0x828) in Ui_Pack_UnloadLayout.

summary: Placeholder class for a group of four secondary-vtable deleting destructors (vtables 0x0076D6A8/0x0076D6E8 and two siblings) that only run the 0x002650C4 Ui window base destructor and free the object; no concrete Ui window class was identified.
evidence: maybe_Ui_Window_SecondaryDeletingDtorA/B 0x0040A374/0x0040BBA4 are 'bl 0x002650C4; b 0x0010F6CC' (Ui window base dtor + free) and 0x0040C3C8/0x0040CCC4 are the same plus one leading store; the secondary vtables are filled only with 0x002650xx base slots and an adjustor, so R3_069 concluded that 'PanelPart' was a placeholder and the concrete class is unidentified.

fields.name: unknown_0x3c
fields.evidence: Real instruction 'str r2, [r0, #0x3c]' at the head of the two byte-identical deleting destructors 0x0040C3C8/0x0040CCC4, but r2 is an undefined third register of a two-argument dtor; no other code touches self+0x3C, so emitted as unknown.

summary: Panel-stack stage class ('g3101_1_out'/'g3101_1_in'/'g3101_2_in'/'g3101_3_in'/'g3101_5_in' animation stages): its virtual slot loads the caller's resource name into the pane mesh and re-applies display mode 4.
evidence: The five batch functions are the same 40-byte virtual slot for the panel-stack stage classes whose descriptors 0x0076E438/0x0076E4F0/0x0076E660 resolve slot +0x74 to the strings 'g3101_2_in'/'g3101_3_in'/'g3101_5_in' (0x007C2AE5/0x007C2AF0/0x007C2B06); each body calls Gfx_SceneNode_LoadMeshByName 0x005F541C with the caller's name and then '(*self+0x40)(self,4)'.

fields.name: unknown_0x100
fields.evidence: No real field: 0x100 = 4 x vtable slot 0x40, because struct_db scaled the slot offset in '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x40))(param_1,4);'. The vtable pointer is *param_1 and none of the five bodies (or the assemble listing) accesses self+0x100.

summary: Item-use result window for a party member: it reads the used item id at +8, rolls the stat boost, applies it to the PartyMember record from func_0035EB98 and pushes the matching result pane.
evidence: Ui_ItemUse_ApplyHpRecovery 0x004C4868 and maybe_Ui_PartyMember_ShowValueChange 0x004D64F8 are the same item-use window: Item_LookupRecord(*(u16*)(self + 8)), Item_RollStatBoostDelta, Ui_Window_PushPane(*(int*)(self + 4) + 0x120, ...) and Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush(*(u32*)(self + 4)); the batch class name comes from these two functions only and should be read as 'item-use result window'.

fields.name: maybe_textSlot1Id
fields.evidence: Ui_PartyMember calls a Ui_Panel base constructor twice; Ui_Panel's four (id, object) text slots put textSlot1Id at +0x14 (S_105, Ui_Panel_SetFourTexts 0x001F044C). The only direct use registers its address in the pane manager ('*(int *)(*(int *)(self + 4) + 0x10cc) = self + 0x14;').

summary: Reference-counted UI resource bundle: four pack handles at +0xC..+0x18 plus one at +0x1C, all released by the destructor, then the 4-word handle array is destroyed.
evidence: Ui_ResourceSet_Dtor 0x002C5A78 writes vtable 0x00760198, loops i = 0..3 over self+0xC (self[i+3]) releasing each non-null handle against the 0x007BA2D0 table with Pack_FreeHandleEntry, calls Pack_ReleaseHandle(self + 7) for +0x1C and std_destroy_range on the 4-word array; its callers are maybe_Ui_SimpleWindow_Dtor and maybe_Ui_HandleSet_Dtor.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: The destructor's first write is '*self = 0x00760198;' - a class vtable literal (Ui_ResourceSet_Dtor 0x002C5A78 is itself reached as a vtable slot), so offset 0 is the vtable pointer.

summary: Small screen-owner record whose Create allocates a 0x328-byte field screen object, hands the word at +0x30 to its constructor and activates the screen through vtable +0x24.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ScreenBase_Create 0x006D6E48 allocates 0x328 bytes with Mem_AllocAligned_2, calls maybe_Field_CreateScreenSystem 0x001772C4 (which is the real constructor and stores its second argument at screen+0x11C), registers the result with Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable and activates it via vtable +0x24; still no caller, so the class role is only inferred.

fields.name: maybe_screenParam
fields.evidence: Passed by value as the second constructor argument in 'maybe_Field_CreateScreenSystem(iVar2, owner + 0x30)' and stored at screen+0x11C (the constructor doc calls that the owner/revision word); no code in this class reads it back, so its purpose is unproven.

summary: Grid scroll/cursor helper: moves the selected row at +0x4C by a delta over an 8-column layout and keeps the paired list pane in sync.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ScrollGrid_MoveCursor 0x006E6180 does 'self[0x13] = self[0x13] + delta', computes (entryCount-1)>>3 as the last row of an 8-column grid, wraps negative values to it and finally calls Ui_List_SelectEntryById / func_001A61FC on the sibling pane at +1; the body is truncated by halt_baddata three times, so the grid identity is not proven.

fields.name: rowIndex
fields.evidence: 'self[0x13] = self[0x13] + delta;' (int element width 4 -> +0x4C) is clamped with 'if (self[0x13] < 0) self[0x13] = iVar5;' where iVar5 = (entryCount-1)>>3 is the last row of an 8-column grid, and the resulting value is fed to Ui_List_SelectEntryById, so it is the selected row index.

summary: Animated 'select__core_loop' selection widget: it plays the select_in/select_out clips and keeps the current Ui animation handle at +0x4C.
evidence: Ui_SelectCoreLoop_Init 0x004E3678 runs the base constructor and binds 'select__core_loop' (0x004E36C8); Ui_SelectCoreLoop_PlayIn 0x004E3600 and PlayOut 0x004E3588 release self->f_4c through vtable +0xC and store the Ui_PlayAnimByName result of 'select_in'/'select_out' back into it.

fields.name: animRef
fields.evidence: self->f_4c holds the Ui_PlayAnimByName result: 'release if != 0 via (**(code **)(**(int **)(self + 4) + 0xc))()', then 'self->f_4c = Ui_PlayAnimByName(*(u32 *)(self + 4), s_select_in_004E3668, 0, 1)' and play through its own vtable +0x54 - the same handle is written by both PlayIn and PlayOut.

summary: Shop item-information window: formats the party gold, the item name and thirteen item stat rows and writes each into a pane through the text getter slot +0x5C.
evidence: Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats 0x00240B6C formats numbers with func_006D3F18 (13 calls: gold digits, bag counts, ownership counts) and writes each row with the text getter '(**(code **)(*self + 0x5c))(self,0x10..0x1e)' followed by func_001A6680(self, page<<16 | paneId, text); values come from the ItemBag at work+0x24A98 via func_00629xxx.

fields.name: unknown_0x170
fields.evidence: No real field: 0x170 = 4 x vtable slot 0x5C ('uVar2 = (**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x5c))(param_1,0x10);' and the 0x12/0x14/0x16/0x18/0x1a/0x1c/0x1e siblings). The vtable pointer is *param_1 and Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats never accesses self+0x170.

summary: Sprite/texture cache: looks a resource name up in the shared Ui_ResourceCache map at +4, creates a missing entry and announces the freshly loaded sprite through vtable +0x18.
evidence: Ui_SpriteCache_LookupOrLoad 0x002F7814 calls func_0065D3D0(self + 1) for the name lookup, Ui_ResourceCache_CreateEntry(self + 1,name) on a miss and then '(**(code **)(*self + 0x18))(self,result,name)' to notify the owner; the cache map itself is the inherited Ui_ResourceCache list head at +4.

fields.name: unknown_0x60
fields.evidence: No real field: 0x60 = 4 x vtable slot 0x18 ('(**(code **)(*self + 0x18))(self,iVar1,param_2);'). The vtable pointer is *self and the only function of this class never accesses self+0x60.

summary: Screen-space sprite marker that points at one actor, builds its billboard basis from the actor transform and restores the actor's attract animation when its motion finishes.
evidence: Ui_SpriteMarker_SetTargetFromActor 0x004772C0 takes the transform with func_00669D88(self->f_28) and the world position floats f_9c/f_a0/f_a4, then calls Gfx_UpdateActorsInViewCone on (work+8)->f_4C with them; maybe_Ui_SpriteMarker_FinishAttract 0x00477310 calls Actor_SelectAttractAnimation(self->f_28,0) when func_00669DD4 reports the motion finished.

fields.name: targetActor
fields.evidence: self->f_28 is passed straight to func_00669D88 (transform), func_00669DD4 (motion-finished query) and Actor_SelectAttractAnimation, and its f_9c/f_a0/f_a4 are read as the world position - the Field_Actor position fields at +0x9C..+0xA4 in structs.json.

summary: Minimal text window initialiser: runs the base constructor and binds the single text pane named 'txt' through vtable +0x34.
evidence: Ui_TextPane_Init 0x00478970 calls the base constructor (drN) and then '(**(code **)(*self + 0x34))(self, 0x4789B0, (u32)*(u16 *)(self + 10) << 0x10, 0)' where 0x4789B0 is the 'txt' literal; the owning screen is unknown.

fields.name: unknown_0xd0
fields.evidence: No real field: 0xD0 = 4 x vtable slot 0x34 ('(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))(param_1,0x4789b0,...)'). The vtable pointer is *param_1 and Ui_TextPane_Init never accesses self+0xD0.
